text:
Continuous Integration, or CI, is a development practice where team members frequently merge their code changes into a shared repository. The core idea is simple: instead of waiting until the end of a project to combine everyone's work, developers integrate their changes several times a day. Every merge triggers an automated build, which compiles the code and runs a series of tests. This process happens within a CI pipeline, a set of automated steps that check the code for errors, style issues, and functionality.

The main benefit of CI is catching issues early. If a change breaks something, the pipeline identifies the problem immediately, allowing developers to fix it right away rather than discovering the bug weeks later. This saves time, reduces stress, and keeps the software stable and reliable throughout development.
